title: Keys an ExternalSecret created are now removed from the target Secret when they leave the template / data

detection.reason: which keys of a target Secret were written by the ExternalSecret is only in the Secret's managedFields, which are not collected

quote: In ALL cases (even when CreationPolicy is Merge), if a data key in the target Secret was created by the ExternalSecret, and it no longer exists in the template (or data/dataFrom), it will be removed from the target secret:
remediation: Before upgrading, compare each ExternalSecret named with its target Secret: any key the ExternalSecret once wrote but no longer renders (from its template, data or dataFrom) is deleted on the first 0.11 reconcile — even with `creationPolicy: Merge`. With `creationPolicy: Owner` the Secret is fully recomputed every loop, so keys other writers added to it are dropped too. Add the keys you still need to the ExternalSecret first.
verifyCommand: kubectl get externalsecrets.external-secrets.io,clusterexternalsecrets.external-secrets.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select((.spec.target.creationPolicy // .spec.externalSecretSpec.target.creationPolicy // "Owner") == "Merge") | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name) target=\(.spec.target.name // .metadata.name)"'  # each row is a Merge-policy ExternalSecret whose shared Secret can lose keys

title: Reconcile rewrite: `--enable-managed-secrets-caching` is the new default; memory use may rise

detection.reason: memory rises when `--enable-secrets-caching` is NOT set — an absent flag cannot be told from one set another way, so the controller workloads are named for a manual check

quote: Memory usage might increase if you are not already using `--enable-secrets-caching`
remediation: On each ESO controller named that does not pass `--enable-secrets-caching`, watch memory after the upgrade and raise its limit if needed: the new default `--enable-managed-secrets-caching` caches the Secrets ESO manages.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.template.spec.containers[]; .image | test("(^|/)(external-secrets/external-secrets|bitnami/external-secrets)([:@]|$)"))) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) \([.spec.template.spec.containers[].args[]?] | map(select(test("caching"))) | join(" "))"'  # each row is an ESO workload and its caching flags

title: CRDs now validate names and keys — objects that skipped required fields are rejected on their next update

detection.reason: schema validation runs at admission; a stored object is only re-validated when it is next written

quote: All of the CRDs now have proper kubebuilder markers for validation. This might surprise someone leaving out some data that was essentially actually required or expected in a certain format. This is now validated in #4104.
remediation: Run your ExternalSecret / SecretStore / PushSecret manifests through a server-side dry run against a 0.11 CRD set (or `kubectl explain`) before upgrading; malformed names or keys that 0.10 stored are refused on the next apply.

title: OLM: 0.11.0 is the last release published to OperatorHub
quote: As of `0.11.0` is the last release available for OLM until further notice.
remediation: If ESO is installed through OLM (OperatorHub Subscription), plan a move to the Helm chart; OLM will not deliver anything after 0.11.0. Upstream notes the 0.11.0 OLM bundle can run newer images by setting `image.tag`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get subscriptions.operators.coreos.com -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.name | test("external-secrets")) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) \(.spec.name)"'  # each row is an OLM subscription to ESO
coversNotes: v0.11.0 (What's Changed): chore: deprecation policy and deprecating process

title: Generators: ClusterGenerator and generator caching change how generators are defined
quote: We added ClusterGenerators and Generator caching as well. This might create some problems in the way generators are defined now.
remediation: Re-check each ExternalSecret named (they use a generator) after the upgrade: generated values are cached per ExternalSecret and generators may now be referenced cluster-wide.
verifyCommand: kubectl get externalsecrets.external-secrets.io,clusterexternalsecrets.external-secrets.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select([(.spec.dataFrom // .spec.externalSecretSpec.dataFrom // [])[]?.sourceRef.generatorRef] | map(select(. != null)) | length != 0) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row is an ExternalSecret that uses a generator
